#3800. Assassin's Creed is reportedly going to ancient Rome, while a mobile spin-off heads to Jerusalem

Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games, and one of them is set in ancient Rome.

That's according to YouTuber Xj0nathan, who says the Rome game is codenamed Mars. He claims two sources with access to Ubisoft's backend systems backed up the information, and that the setting will likely be linked to the upcoming Assassin's Creed TV series.

The second game, codenamed Pocket, is said to be a mobile title set in Jerusalem. Xj0nathan claims it'll play a bit like Assassin’s Creed Valhalla’s Mastery Challenge, and look similar to the most recent Prince of Persia. The hero's mentor is apparently a character called Myriam.

Insider Gaming says it's heard the codenames too, but couldn't confirm them well enough to report them independently. It puts some of that down to the turbulence the franchise has gone through since former Assassin's Creed boss Marc-Alexis Côté left Ubisoft.

Last month, the outlet's sources also claimed Assassin's Creed Hexe, the next mainline game, had been delayed internally by another year, likely to 2028. Other reports claim we'll see it next year.

If Mars does move into full production, don't hold your breath - Insider Gaming doesn't expect us to hear anything about it until 2029 or 2030.

Assassin's Creed has visited Rome before, in 2010’s Brotherhood, but that was the Renaissance version of the city.

The leak comes less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

Rebel Wolves has confirmed that The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting New Game+ as part of its 1.2 update next week.

Despite a number of nominations and bringing out one of the best vampire games of the modern era, The Blood of Dawnwalker didn't pick up any awards at the Golden Joystick Awards this week. It did come close, with a second place finish in PC Game of the Year and Best Storytelling, and a fifth place finish in Ultimate Game of the Year. The ex-CD Projekt Red devs at Rebel Wolves were happy with their performance, and clearly haven't let the narrow losses faze them, as the game's next major patch is coming very soon.

As announced by Rebel Wolves on Reddit, The Blood of Dawnwalker 1.2 update releases next week. This update will include balance changes with enemy health pools and ability use being tweaked as well as terrain adjustments to improve movement around the world. But the headline act of this new update is New Game+ finally arriving in the game.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+." the post reads. As part of this mode, the level cap is being raised to 100, with enemies balanced and scaled accordingly. On top of that, items will receive New Game+ versions with updated stats, too.

The average playthrough of The Blood of Dawnwalker is around 25 hours according to HowLongToBeat, so this new addition should help you get even more out of what is considered "short" by RPG standards.

#3798. Crusader Kings publishers Paradox announce CEO swap, say they're "in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges"

"My plan was never to be CEO for life", says man clearly not embracing the grand strategy despot spirit

Paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have announced plans to switch overlords early next year. Fredrik Wester will make way for Mattias Lilja, as the deputy CEO takes the throne.

While the move's been announced this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a new figurehead in place as the calendars swap. Departing CEO Fredrik Wester isn't going far, at least for now, as he'll "continue focusing on the company's long-term development as a member of the board".

"My plan was never to be CEO for life," Wester said. "The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the company’s journey. Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over."

"The Board wants to thank Fredrik for his visionary leadership and outstanding contributions over these years," stated chairman Håkan Sjunnesson. "As a result, Paradox is in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges." He added that Lilja is "more than ready to assume the role and lead Paradox towards new gaming experiences that last for decades".

Lilja himself declared that Paradox have "a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games" and will be "stepping up the pace". "We will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus," he said.

As Wester alluded to, he previously served as Paradox CEO from 2009 to 2018, with a brief stint as executive chairman of the board sandwiched between that and his latest stint as CEO since 2021. Lilja has been deputy CEO since 2024 and chief of staff since 2021, having originally joined Paradox as a producer in 2009.

The past half decade has been a very mixed bag for Paradox. Their big strategy flagships keep ticking along, albeit with the question of whether their next DLC will feel worth it hovering overhead near-permanently. Outside of that, however, the likes of Cities: Skylines 2, Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2, and cancelled Sims competitor Life By You have made for a track record heavy on questionable decisions and games which either flopped hard or failed to blow away expectations. Wester acknowledged back in 2024 that the company had "made the wrong calls in several projects, especially outside of our core".

With the likes of post-apocalyptic strategy game Afterworld currently in the works, it'll be interesting to see if Lilja's tenure can see Paradox finally start to nail not just their nerdy bread and butter, but also games that don't involve staring down at a big map.

#3797. Sony delays PlayStation's Pulse Elevate speakers indefinitely, less than a week before launch

Sony has delayed its Pulse Elevate wireless speakers indefinitely, less than a week before they were due to launch.

The news came in a 6th November update to Sony’s original announcement on the PlayStation Blog, first spotted by IGN. Quality testing has turned up a "production issue", Sony said, and there's no new release date yet.

"As part of our ongoing quality testing of Pulse Elevate speakers, we have identified a production issue with the product and have made the decision to delay the launch," the statement reads. "The additional time will allow us to ensure the product will deliver the experience we intended for our players. We apologise for the delay and appreciate your patience and understanding. We look forward to bringing Pulse Elevate to players soon."

The speakers were set to go on sale worldwide on 12th November, and pre-orders opened in September. It's unclear what, exactly, happens to those orders, but we'll update as and when we find out more.

Sony revealed Pulse Elevate in September 2025 as its first wireless speakers for desktop gaming. They sit alongside the Pulse Elite headset and Pulse Explore earbuds, and cost £199.99 ($219.99).

They connect to PS5, PC, Mac, and PlayStation Portal via PlayStation Link, and can pair with a phone over Bluetooth at the same time. There's also a microphone in the right speaker with what Sony calls "AI-enhanced noise rejection".

Midnight Black was due to be available everywhere, while the White version was limited to a handful of countries, including the UK.

Alongside the Pulse Elevate speakers, Sony revealed a range of hardware in September 2025, including a 27-inch gaming monitor that's coming only to the US and Japan.

Doom developer id Software has confirmed that it's working on a new game, although in phrasing that might strike you as familiar, it'll be "some time" before it's ready to reveal anything.

The new project at id was first announced by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who's been making a few posts on X today to mark the looming 25th anniversary of the original Xbox console. "Few studios have shaped the first-person shooter genre as much as id Software," Sharma wrote. "Slaughter Mode comes to Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations on Monday, and the team is already working on its next game."

"Already" might be stretching it a bit: The studio's previous game, Doom: The Dark Ages, came out well over a year ago, although the Revelations expansion only dropped in July. Regardless, the studio replied to Sharma's post to confirm that yes, a new game is coming.

"We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin," the studio said. "It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on."

@asha_shar We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.November 12, 2026

If that rings a bell, you may be thinking of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, which was given an official subtitle earlier this month—eight years after it was first announced. Despite that passage of time, Bethesda warned that more waiting is in store, using exactly the same phrase as id: "It'll be some time before we're ready to share more."

Of course id Software and Bethesda Softworks are both subsidiaries of ZeniMax Media, which is owned by Xbox, so maybe that shared turn of phrase isn't entirely surprising. It does feel a bit unfortunate, though.

On the other hand, it's nice to have confirmation that id is in fact doing something new. The studio was hit hard by the Xbox layoffs in July, reportedly losing more than 130 employees, raising concerns about its ability to continue functioning as a standalone developer. Studio co-director Marty Stratton said in October that "there was a very deliberate effort [during the layoffs] to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do." Stratton also said id is now "working more closely with MachineGames than ever," leading to speculation that the two studios may be collaborating on Wolfenstein 3.

#3794. Star Wars Zero Company studio Bit Reactor lays off staff, a month after bringing furloughed developers back

"While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together."

Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work.

Several developers announced on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin. Bit Reactor hasn't said how many people are affected.

Among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough. UI engineer Tyler Eichten, who worked on much of the on-screen UI for the game's tactical missions, and Ryan Mosher from the QA team have also confirmed they were let go.

"While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote. "It was a privilege to ship a game with you."

Bit Reactor furloughed most of its staff in the weeks before Zero Company launched on 27th August, with one source putting the figure at roughly 80 percent. The studio appeared to have run out of money just short of release.

The game did well regardless, and is thought to have sold more than a million copies within a month. Then, in a message shared on Bluesky on 7th October, CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio had "started the process of returning more of our team back to work". Asking staff to step away so close to launch was "an incredibly difficult decision", he said, "but one that was necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible".

It's thought more than half the studio returned, though not everyone went back on full pay. It's not clear whether any of those who returned were among the people laid off this week.

In Eurogamer's Star Wars Zero Company review, we awarded the game four out of five stars, saying, "an already winning genre is matched with the perfect setting in this earnest, heartfelt, smart and slightly ramshackle turn-based tactics gem".

#3793. Worst Class Ever takes asymmetrical multiplayer back to school, with a teacher player trying to spot the naughty children among the NPCs

Master the sinful art of eating sweets behind your textbook

What's the best prank you ever pulled on a teacher in school, assuming you went to school? By which I mean, a genuinely funny prank that didn't cause any injuries, break any of the more important laws (legal or ethical), or leave anybody with years of mental distress.

I'll start: I once had to write a four-page punishment essay with the topic "silence is golden", after being caught talking in class. I took the essay very seriously for the first three pages, only to end it with the phrase "...but not as golden as my arse." The teacher who set me the essay smugly tore it up without reading it - as I knew he would. Checkmate, Mr Thompson. Decades later, the last laugh remains mine.

Worst Class Ever is a new don't-call-it-friendslop asymmetrical multiplayer game dedicated to such larks. One player is a teacher, and seven others are naughty delinquent children, hiding in amongst some well-brought-up and obedient NPCs. As the wayward tykes, your goal is to do mischievous things like eating at your desk, passing notes, dropping banana skins, and playing on your phone, without being spotted by Teach.

All of this takes place in a breezy modern Japanese high school, the kind familiar from a million animes. Bagsy the Protagonist Desk by the window at the back of the class! The maplist spans the curriculum, from computer labs to gym tracks to stepped lecture theatres. I don't think there are any covert edu-tainment mechanics, but if you're playing Teacher, I guess there's nothing to stop you actually explaining the periodic table while trying to work out who keeps throwing chalk at your head.

What a wholesome and whimsical place! Such happy memories! Oh crikey, the male teacher is terrifying – why can't he stop grinning? And why do I have a smoke grenade? Why is this lesson taking place in the dark? Why are the teachers permitted to punch the students and tie them to wooden posts? Worst Class Ever definitely isn't a horror game, but I'm not sure I'd send my kids to this particular institution. I feel like we're one texture pack away from playing a more sociable version of Little Nightmares. Read more on Steam.

He wasn't fond of the workaround in the DLC either

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Oftentimes in game development, you can't be sure how something will work until you ship. In the case of Skyrim, one of the leads was certain the level cap wouldn't be a problem, and then players made it clear he had the wrong idea.

Bruce Nesmith, lead designer on Skyrim and a former longtime developer at Bethesda, told the Examined Game podcast all about his logic. "When creating the system where all the different skills would go to 100, it implied, mathematically, a level limit of 81," he explains.

"I didn't think of that," he says. "Most of the games that Bethesda produces are designed to, you've played all the content roughly around level 50. That's what we shoot for."

He qualifies this with the caveat that that's a broad generalisation, because it depends on how the players approach the game. The amount of stealth or magic you use can impact things, but you'll likely still be in the ballpark of level 50 by the time you've seen the bulk of any given Bethesda release.

"So, 81, and what do I care?" Nesmith continues. "I was wrong. The players didn't want to finish playing their character at 81 and start a new one. They had a character they loved, why couldn't they keep playing?"

This seems like a by-product of creating something as wildly popular as Skyrim. Few games will ever be as widely enjoyed and played as The Elder Scrolls 5, and that means there are plenty of people who wish the whole experience was longer.

There was a course correction, as Nesmith points out, in the Dragonborn DLC, where you could reset skills by spending Dragon Souls. This was introduced in a free update with Legendary Mode afterward.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

"It wasn't my favorite mechanic the way we did it," Nesmith states. "But it worked." That it did, and it didn't slow down the RPG's momentum at all. Whatever else Bethesda's planning for The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, I doubt there'll be a level cap, because it sounds like the team learned their lesson.

"We don't want that scenario": Skyrim had to change a major Oblivion problem, but will Todd Howard's "elegant solution" make it to The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel?

#3790. While soulslikes went bigger than big, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the big, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives.

Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

Still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

Which is welcome, as these big lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

Recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

#3789. WoW: Forever is the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history, says Blizzard

World of Warcraft: Forever is the biggest launch in the MMO's history, pulling in more concurrent players than any previous WoW launch.

Blizzard shared the news on social media yesterday (7th November), saying the new edition, which launched on 4th November, broke records for both peak concurrent players and returning players.

"Congratulations everyone, you made history!" the official World of Warcraft account posted. "This is all because of you, the players. From all of us, thank you!"

The game hasn't just tempted back lapsed players. In a follow-up post, executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale said it brought in the most new players for a WoW launch in 15 years.

"Welcome all! We're so happy you're here experiencing Azeroth for the first time alongside those of us playing it for the first time... again," she wrote.

Wooo! Another statistic is filling our hearts -- we are seeing the most NEW players for a WoW launch in 15 YEARS!Welcome all! We’re so happy you’re here experiencing Azeroth for the first time alongside those of us playing it for the first time...AGAIN 😁 #WoWForever https://t.co/QPp3MDoVyr

Blizzard finally officially confirmed World of Warcraft: Forever at September's BlizzCon after fans were obsessing over colours as dataminers pulled hues from Blizzard's website that were labelled under a curious "wow 2" tag, leading many to speculate that this referred to the rumoured World of Warcraft Camelot, or as it's better known, "Classic Plus", much like how Blizzard is now expanding Diablo 2.

Blizzard hasn't shared any actual player numbers yet.

World of Warcraft: Forever's first major hotfix patch - which, among other things, has put an end to an especially powerful bug that tipped PvP battlegrounds like Warsong Gulch to the Horde's advantage - rolled out on Friday.

Amid the countless PTO requests and conspicuously-timed doctor appointment notices targeting November 19, one game studio's employees have been absolved of the need to provide themselves an alibi on Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day. Pocketpair announced on X today that all of its employees "have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA 6 launches."

"On November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin," Pocketpair wrote in a memo announcing the company holiday. "At Pocketpair, we believe such a historic occasion deserves our full attention."

All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA6 launches. Please see the attached notice for details. https://t.co/qJjJ7IvhhYNovember 12, 2026

From November 19 to November 23, "all employees who intend to play Grand Theft Auto 6" at Pocketpair will be "excused from their regular duties and are instead encouraged to undertake a business trip to Vice City." Technically, since that time spans a weekend, it's only really granting three days of holiday time. But, you know, who's counting?

The studio also made sure to note that work is proceeding on updates for Palworld and Craftopia, which are "expected to be carried out as scheduled," presumably in an effort to preempt anyone who might be reaching for their torches and pitchforks.

Pocketpair's not the only company providing those on its payroll with some well-timed time off. Earlier this week, Logitech announced Logi Game Day, offering its 7,000 employees a day off to "formally" recognize "the cognitive and professional benefits of gaming"—which the company has chosen to acknowledge on November 19, specifically.

Robin Piispanen, general manager of the Logitech G gaming brand, did say employees are free to play whatever game they want, though. Corporate benevolence knows no bounds.

Outside of the immediate gaming industry ecosystem, California-based automotive performance parts manufacturer Burger Motorsports announced on its Instagram that it will be "observing a temporary company-wide operational pause" on GTA 6's launch day, after determining that "normal business operations may be impacted." Likewise, Canadian truck manufacturer Edison Motors opted to grant its employees a four-day weekend beginning on November 19.

#3787. Cyberpunk trading sim Probably Stolen is getting three big updates with new starting scenarios - organ trading, junk empires and fine dining

Mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three big updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each update may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

Coming up in mid-December, there's the Junker starting scenario, which I assume is all about trading scrap, rather than being a Prussian nobleman. You'll get a bespoke perk, new items, and the ability to hire, equip and send scavs on expeditions. This update will also include some minor expansions for the Fence and Gunsmith vocations – the latter will be able to flog or otherwise make use of shotgun shells, 25mm grenade rounds and a tier 3 handmade SMG, alongside new armour.

Late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major update. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

Last but not least, the planned April update will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

Are you playing Probably Stolen? It's been doing better than expected. I was keen on the demo, but my attention was lured away by a truly upsetting game about dogpeople in caves.

#3786. Missing teenager rescued after reaching out to another player in Among Us

"Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim."

A teenager who went missing in Utah more than 17 months ago has been rescued from a home in Oregon after she got in touch with another young player in Among Us.

According to a federal criminal complaint reported by Newsweek and KUTV (via IGN), the girl, who was 15 when she disappeared from Garden City, Utah, on 29th May 2025, began chatting with another teenager in Among Us on or around 15th October this year.

The pair later moved their conversation to a different social media app, where she told them who she was and that she was being held against her will in Oregon. She had been given a phone with no cellular data, which meant she could only get online via wi-fi.

The other teen told their parent, who contacted the FBI on 1st November. Agents listened in on a video call between the parent and the girl, and she was recovered from the house later that day. She is now 17.

Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, of Huntington, Oregon, was arrested during a traffic stop.

According to the US Attorney's Office for the District of Utah, he allegedly met the girl online in May 2025, then drove to Utah to pick her up and took her back to his home across state lines. He was charged on 2nd November with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity, and made his first court appearance in Boise, Idaho, on 4th November.

"Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim," said US Attorney Melissa Holyoak. "Those who allegedly exploit and prey upon the most vulnerable members of our communities will be relentlessly investigated and held accountable."

Utah's US Attorney's Office stresses that a complaint is merely an allegation, and that all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

It's that time of year when all the retailers start early-launching their Black Friday deals. The last 24 hours have seen Nintendo, Walmart, Secretlab, and now Best Buy kicking off their Black Friday offerings, but not all are made equal. In fact, after scouring the shelves at Best Buy, we've only found one Xbox Series X controller that's at a low enough price to recommend, and it's the same price at Amazon.

Fret not, gamers, because it just so happens that it's the weekend before the arrival of GTA 6, and the Xbox gamepad in question is one I've already recommended this week in my roundup of the best controllers for GTA 6.

It might be the best of a weaker selection of deals at Best Buy, but it's one I'd still happily recommend to gamers for the second time in a week - whether they're returning to video games for the first time in years, or they're sprucing up their setup to mark the occasion.

The controller is the Nacon Revolution X Unlimited, which is usually priced at $200, but is currently sitting at its lowest cost since January of this year. For context, it's what I deem the best controller overall for the Xbox Series X, PC, and now, thanks to the arrival of its sibling, the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited, the PS5 as well.

You're getting a hell of a bargain with the RXU dropping to $150. It's got Hall effect thumbsticks (which have more precision than a standard controller and are immune to stick drift), six extra buttons for you to map, and a screen and menu system built into the gamepad itself.

It also comes in a carry case with weights you can add to the grips, thumbstick width adjustments, different thumbstick tops, a cable, a charging stand, and a wireless dongle. You're getting a lot for your money here - especially when more recent options like the SteelSeries Aeon Pro are trying to charge you $100 more than this for a very similar product.

Whether you go for Amazon or Best Buy is up to you. At Amazon, you can get the RXU in either its original black colorway or in its special Xbox 360 Anniversary variant for the same $149.99 price. At Best Buy, I'm only seeing the original black version at that price.

Why would I recommend it for GTA 6? Well, it's obviously going to only be useful for Xbox players at the moment until Rockstar remembers how big the PC gaming market is, so keep that in mind. But the RXU has a lot of premium feel to it, which goes hand-in-hand with a blockbuster game you're probably going to set aside a good chunk of time to play.

Of all the controllers I've reviewed, the RXU has the best-feeling microswitch buttons I've found. A super light actuation, a short travel distance, a really satisfying, almost mouse-like click, with the sort of membrane cushioning feel you'd enjoy if you're used to Xbox and PS5 controllers from the olden days. It's also perfect if you have larger hands since it's quite a chunky controller that offers crunchy feedback through its motors. And its triggers are well-shaped for all the driving you'll do around Vice City.

Want a faster response when you're shooting? The microswitch trigger stops will see to that.

For more, take a look at the best PS5 controllers, the best PC controllers, and the best TMR controllers. We're also rounding up the best headsets for GTA 6 as well.

#3782. Saving Mass Effect would take $200m+, says BioWare co-founder

Anyone hoping to buy Mass Effect from EA and finish what BioWare started needs to get saving now, as it could cost over $200 million (£150m).

That's according to BioWare co-founder Trent Oster, who reckons that's what a new Mass Effect game would need to meet fans' expectations.

"The scary component of Mass Effect is the audience is going to want the best of 'AAA' development," Oster said on Twitter/X, as spotted by GamesRadar.

The scary component of Mass Effect is the audience is going to want the best of “AAA” development. Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200M+. That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work.

"Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200M+. That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work."

He did add that it could be done for less, though. "That said, I think it can be done well for less than that amount with a disciplined approach and an experienced team," Oster said.

"I think a game could be done cheaper, if you kept it simple and hit the big beats," he added in a separate tweet. "It wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept. The big push would be getting the IP free. The fans deserve more than one game."

I think a game could be done cheaper, if you kept it simple and hit the big beats. It wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept. The big push would be getting the IP free. The fans deserve more than one game.

Oster's comments come as the #SaveMassEffect campaign continues to grow following EA's decision to close BioWare and cancel Mass Effect 5. Fans want EA to keep making Mass Effect games, or hand the series over to a studio that will.

Oster has backed the campaign too. "I love seeing all the energy around #SaveMassEffect," he wrote on 4th November. "I think there is a still a great thesis for a well-funded RPG developer who can deliver. Makes me want to get some of the original band back together."

EA has not confirmed whether or not it would consider selling the IP.

The petition created to save BioWare's well-loved sci-fi RPG, Mass Effect, topped 185,000 signatures in just days. It's now exceeded 317,000. Joe Smith, credited with starting the petition, isn't necessarily asking EA to change its mind about BioWare; instead, the petition calls for "decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect".

We said a sad farewell to BioWare last month. The closure, which came just months after Saudi Arabia's $55bn leveraged buyout of EA, was anticipated by experts, but drew widespread condemnation and messages of sympathy from across the industry.

A new report claims EA closed BioWare because it was forced to choose between investing in one of two sci-fi projects: a new Mass Effect game or a new Star Wars Battlefront game. And it chose the latter.

Fans are trying other routes to keep BioWare's doors open, too. Canadian fans of the studio have escalated their grievances to the governmental level, calling on the Canadian Government to step in and save the studio from closure, seemingly after Canada's New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis called on the government to do so.

Team Meat has announced Super Meat Boy Again+, a game described as “everything you remember from Super Meat Boy presented through the wonderful lens of nostalgia with stuff added to it,” including new art, music, cutscenes, levels, secrets, and unlockables. It will be available for PC via Steam. A release date was not announced.

Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page:

Super Meat Boy is a tough as nails platformer originally released to much fanfare and great acclaim in 2010. It is held as a gold standard in difficult but fair platforming. You play as Meat Boy, a boy with no skin who leaves blood everywhere, who is saving his girlfriend, Bandage Girl, from Dr. Fetus, a fetus in a jar wearing a top hat and a monocle.

Super Meat Boy Again+ everything you remember from Super Meat Boy presented through the wonderful lens of nostalgia with stuff added to it. Everything is new but familiar. We have new art, new music, new cutscenes, new secrets, and new stuff.

Since 2010, millions of people played Super Meat Boy, all the secrets are known, all the levels are mastered, all the characters unlocked, so we have to give fans familiar with the game something to pull their hair out over. That’s the “+” in Again+, and no, we won’t spoil it. You’ll go into it blind like you did the first time you played Super Meat Boy.

For our old fans, we want to present the game as you remember it through the wonderful lens of nostalgia.

For our new fans, we want to give you a great looking, easy to pick up but difficult to master platformer that you may have missed because it came out like four years after YouTube was invented.

The upcoming Fable reboot is set to launch on February 23, 2027, and with that date growing inexorably closer Xbox has dropped a new gameplay trailer showcasing four minutes of heroic questing across a rather grim-looking slice of Albion.

The trailer shows off a little bit of everything: some cinematics, some chitchat, the UI, and of course plenty of combat: melee, ranged, and even a bit of magic.

Today we're sharing four minutes of new @fable gameplay. It's been a long road to bring this franchise back, and I'm proud of the work Playground Games is doing. Take a look. https://t.co/q74VcEt5xENovember 12, 2026

"The Hero of Briar Hill has entered the depths of Deepwood alongside Arden, a local Hero, to investigate why strange magical happenings have been troubling the people of Oakshire. Here, they cross a threshold where the natural magic of Deepwood appears corrupted by an outside force, and they discover hints as to who or what could be responsible..."

The reaction to the video is quite positive among the YouTube comments but somewhat more subdued on the PC Gaming subreddit, where more than one poster suggested that it doesn't really show the game in its best light—which is to say that it doesn't really look like Fable, or at least what Fable fans expected. Fable 3 may not be everyone's favorite game in the series but it was bright, colorful, exuberant—this video, by comparison, seems downright grim and conventional.

That's about where I land on it: A four-minute clip obviously isn't going to tell the whole story, but with the video being showcased as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary, and the full Fable release now just three months away (unless it's delayed again), it's reasonable to assume that Playground and Xbox would want to put their best foot forward. And, well, this is fine, but I can't say it has me all charged up to play Fable: To me, it just feels kind of flat.

But maybe that's just me—we'll find out in February. Fable on the PC is available for pre-purchase now on Steam.

The CEO of the publishers behind GTA 6, Take-Two Interactive, isn't quite ready to go on his victory lap just yet, but he is once again enjoying what he thinks might be the most valuable entertainment IP in the world.

Speaking to David Rubenstein, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked about the size of of GTA 6's impending launch. In traditional fashion, Zelnick remained pretty humble, telling Rubenstein that "we never claim success before it occurs."

In this instance, he notes, Take-Two and Rockstar have had plenty of success together. "It's true that GTA 5 was a massive hit," he admits. "It sold in over 230 million units, and we believe the Grand Theft Auto franchise as a whole is probably the most valuable intellectual property in the entertainment business, of any type, because of its enormous reach to consumers worldwide."

Zelnick's argument is a potent one, but it's also a little hard to pin down. Off the top of my head, Pokémon and Marvel have certainly generated more money, but that's admittedly off the back of many hundreds more releases (and many more decades, in Marvel's case). Clearly, however, neither of those franchises can match the billions of dollars off a single launch that GTA 6 is set to make next week, or the other billions that the long tail of GTA Online is likely to secure. Pound-for-pound, GTA certainly sends those other heavyweights back to the corner, even if the 13-year gap between releases might be hurting a little.

Despite his quiet confidence in the brand, however, Zelnick is still refusing to count his chickens before they hatch. "The team at Rockstar has been working diligently to try to create something extraordinary with Grand Theft Auto 6," he says. "I believe they will, I'm very optimistic, but as for success, we'll have to wait until November 19 and beyond."

#3778. Phasmophobia players raise over $230,000 for heart charity, more than double last year's total

The Phasmophobia community has raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

Developer Kinetic Games announced the final figure for this year's Ghost Hunts for Hearts event on 6th November. The charity drive ran from 26th October to 2nd November, and more than 500 streamers signed up to take part. That's the biggest turnout yet for a creator fundraiser run by Heart Liive, the American Heart Association's streaming initiative.

Last year's event raised a little over $100,000.

Congratulations, Ghost Hunters, you've surpassed the community target and raised over $200,000 for our friends at @Heart_Liive!Your kindness and generosity will not go unrewarded, log in to Phasmophobia before the 15th November to claim the Animated AHA Advocate ID Card &… pic.twitter.com/KFQKaqXNCl

Streamers who fundraised could hand out an event-exclusive Advocate ID Card and Badge to their viewers as a Twitch Drop. Kinetic set a target of $200,000 at the start of the week, and once players sailed past it, an animated version of the card and badge set unlocked for all.

"The Phasmophobia community never fails to amaze us, and this year they've outdone themselves," said Tom Dent, lead social media and player experience manager at Kinetic Games. "Thank you to every streamer, viewer and player who took part."

Phasmophobia launched in Early Access in September 2020, and sends teams of up to four players into haunted locations to gather evidence of what's lurking there.

The studio also launched a publishing arm, Kinetic Publishing, earlier this year. Its first game, the starship job simulator Contact Protocol, is due out in spring 2027.

Phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027, as the studio said it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Update. The studio ended up apologising to players for issues with the long-awaited update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

#3777. Missed something on your first go around The Blood of Dawnwalker? I've got good news, as next week's update adds in new game plus

A big part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 update next week that adds in a new game plus mode.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

In any case, the update goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration."

Overall, a bit of a smaller update compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something important or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests."

Earlier this year, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma revealed on Twitter that she'd seen The Elder Scrolls 6. Now, she's announcing that MachineGames is making Wolfenstein 3 with a photo of the script attached to a tweet. I don't miss E3, but it feels like a step down in terms of spectacle to go from on-stage trailer reveals to an executive just tweeting it out.

Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. https://t.co/YyX8LrbTvhNovember 12, 2026

MachineGames followed up a few minutes later with their own tweet, saying, "His reputation precedes him. Wolfenstein 3 is in production." As well as the same photo of the script, they attached a photo of Debra Wilson (who played Resistance cell leader Grace Walker in The New Colossus) recording motion-capture.

It's been a couple of years since Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, though MachineGames did release a Quake expansion for its 30th anniversary in the meantime. A page of script and a photo of a motion-capture session doesn't tell us much about how far along it is, but I wouldn't expect it super soon. It'd be nice to have something to tie into the upcoming Wolfenstein TV series coming from the same folks as the Fallout show.

In a follow-up message, Bethesda confirmed that along with Wilson returning as Walker, Brian Bloom will also be back in the role of series lead BJ Blazkowicz.

What do we think they'll subtitle Wolfenstein 3? MachineGames has an opportunity to really mess with our Steam libraries by calling it "Wolfenstein 3D".

#3775. Ocarina of Time remake datamine suggests Master Quest is on the way

Ocarina of Time's notoriously tricky Master Quest mode could be making a comeback in the new remake.

Dataminer MrCheeze shared a list of strings from the remake's files on Bluesky, several of which tie the tag "MQ" to dungeons like Dodongo's Cavern.

In a follow-up, as spotted by TheGamer, they pointed to further entries, including "HasMQ", "IsMQModeExist", "NewGameMQ", and "ReleaseMQ".

Fellow dataminer OatmealDome added on Twitter/X that the mode will be unlocked by owning DLC, rather than arriving in an update, though "the data is incomplete". "I can confirm that the world is mirrored and dungeons are modified (e.g. cows in Jabu-Jabu's Belly)," they said.

If you've not played it, Master Quest is a remixed version of Ocarina of Time with rearranged dungeons and tougher puzzles. It first appeared as a bonus disc on GameCube, then came back in 2011's Ocarina of Time 3D, which unlocked it after you finished the main game. That version also mirrored the whole world, which matches what OatmealDome has found, and had enemies deal double damage.

[Ocarina of Time] #ootspoilersThere is data in the game files for Master Quest. It will be unlocked by *owning DLC* - it is not just an update.The data is incomplete, but I can confirm that the world is mirrored and dungeons are modified (e.g. cows in Jabu-Jabu's Belly).

As with any datamine, there's no guarantee it'll ever see the light of day. Nintendo hasn't announced any DLC for the remake, and it's not clear whether Master Quest would be free, like it was on 3DS, or paid.

The Ocarina of Time remake launched on Switch 2 on 5th November. Donlan called the new version an "astonishing remake" in his five-star Eurogamer Ocarina of Time review.

#3774. From 2D to 3D and back to 2D again, the original platforming classic Super Meat Boy returns with a slick remaster complete with new levels and too many old saws

Earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a new dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

What is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a big new lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff."

If the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

There's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an update there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as big a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the new one on Steam.

Grace Ashcroft, the freshly minted protagonist of Resident Evil Requiem, has all the makings of a great video game scream queen. She overcomes immense adversity even while suffering a severe anxiety condition and she's the new face of one of the most iconic franchises in horror gaming. Capcom has yet to outright confirm she'll return in future Resident Evil games, but the actor who portrays her seems to think she will.

Grace actor Angela Sant'Albano recently took home the Golden Joystick Award for Best Lead Performer, and with Resident Evil Requiem having won Ultimate Game of the Year, it was a big night for the actor. We caught up with her during the event, and she shared her hopes for the future of Grace Ashcroft.

"I would really love to see how her relationship with Leon blossoms," Sant'Albano tells us. "I think we have a beautiful mentorship, almost brotherly, sisterly relationship brewing. And I also want to know what happens with her and Emily." Sant'Albano says she's developed a close friendship with Emily actor Emma Rose, and she wants to see Grace take on "a more maternal role and see how she carries that forward."

Throughout the absolute nightmare that Grace endures through Resident Evil Requiem, she evolves from a state of anxiety-induced paralysis to having just enough confidence to shakily defend herself with a gun, and Sant'Albano is looking forward to seeing her reach her full potential, even if she'll never be an action hero like Leon Kennedy.

"I don't think she'll ever be a Leon character. She's never going to be badass, you know, doing roundhouse kicks," she says. "But I do think her courage and her self-esteem will grow the more that she trusts herself and forgives herself for a lot of the things that I think tie her down. So I think there's a long way to go with her."

Resident Evil Veronica, a remake of Code Veronica, is the next big Resident Evil game to come after Requiem, and I think it's safe to say we won't see any Grace Ashcroft. Capcom has yet to reveal the next mainline installment, but after Sant'Albano's win at the Golden Joysticks, I think I can speak for Resident Evil fans everywhere when I say she's a fan-favorite to return in later entries.

The Last of Us inspired Resident Evil 7's course correction because the devs "wanted the critical acclaim other games were garnering," ex-Capcom senior dev says

#3772. How to unlock Flounder and Sebastian in Disney Dreamlight Valley The Keepsake Sea

The collection of characters from The Little Mermaid is growing, with Ariel’s beloved fish friends Flounder and Sebastian joining the village in Disney Dreamlight Valley. The process for unlocking them looks vastly different from all other villagers, though, and can be tricky to navigate.

If you’re hoping to get every character available to find and meet around the valley, figuring out what needs to be done to recruit these two is essential. Here’s how to unlock Flounder and Sebastian in Disney Dreamlight Valley.

Flounder and Sebastian can be unlocked by purchasing either the Deluxe Edition or the Ultimate Edition of The Keepsake Sea in DDV. These two Adventure Companions are exclusive content locked behind these special variants of the Expansion Pass, which means you must buy one of the two to get them.

With either of these versions purchased, you’ll then be able to unlock Flounder and Sebastian in DDV. These two are likely locked behind a few quests, probably ones that require you to first unlock Ariel and progress through part of The Keepsake Sea’s storyline to learn about Adventure Companions. We’ll provide an update here on all additional unlock requirements once they’re available to tackle.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Flounder and Sebastian will very likely only ever be available as exclusive bonus content unlocked for purchasing either the Deluxe Edition or the Ultimate Edition of The Keepsake Sea DLC. Most other DLCs have had similar exclusivity systems for special game editions, like Sven as an exclusive mount with the Deluxe Edition of Wishblossom Ranch.

All items included in special editions have never been available in any other way. This system has been in place for years, so it’s unlikely to change in the future. This means that the only way to get Flounder and Sebastian in your valley is by buying one of the two DLC game versions that include them.

Flounder and Sebastian are Adventure Companions, not full-on villagers in DDV. This means they act as a hybrid between a Companion and a villager. These special Companions can be given gifts, have daily discussions, and come with their own set of rewards, but are not quite as built out as villagers.

#3771. Congratulations to people who feel mean shooting random NPCs, because GTA 6 tries "to provide mechanisms that encourage" empathy

When you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a new interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

"Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a new interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to."

I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

In any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

#3770. COD: Modern Warfare 4 gets a surprisingly sudden free trial, so you can see what the game's extraction mode DMZ is like

Activision has released the first trial for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's extraction mode DMZ. The trial is available across PC (Steam / Battlenet), PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S until Wednesday, 11th November.

The free trial only includes access to DMZ and no other part of Modern Warfare 4, such as multiplayer or the campaign. And while it's not uncommon for Call of Duty titles to make some of their modes available for free for a limited time, the timing of this DMZ taster is notable.

DMZ launched days before Modern Warfare 4's 23rd October release date, meaning this first trial has arrived just two weeks after the game's full launch. By comparison, Black Ops 7's Endgame mode had its first free trial months after launch, in the game's third season. That said, Endgame continued to be freely available until Season 6.

The DMZ trial also coincides with the launch of Modern Warfare 4's iteration of free-to-play Call of Duty battle royale mode Warzone, and Season 1. Indeed, both DMZ and the new Warzone take place on the same Hajin map, so even if you don't decide to buy the full game to continue playing DMZ, some of that map knowledge will certainly transfer to Warzone.

The DMZ trial does not appear to have any limits, meaning you can climb the ranks, access Story Missions - the only way to play PvE, with caveats - and complete Orders to your heart's content. That includes X01, the new endgame dungeon-like area available to experienced and fully-equipped players.

DMZ players who've been asking Infinity Ward to offer a PvE-only playlist of the PvPvE mode will certainly be happy with the influx of new players, as they could potentially amplify their calls for a PvP-free playlist.

Welcome to the new era, folks, where we increasingly seem to be heading closer to a daily coin flip over whether our core online services stay live or go down. This time, it's Microsoft. Down Detector reports problems with Microsoft 365 services since about 12:30 pm (ET) yesterday, November 12, and issues are still ongoing.

Countries across the world are affected, and some institutions have been affected severely. Parts of the UK government, for instance, are having problems sending and receiving emails. The UK's health service, the NHS, has reportedly said it is unable to access online consultation for patients. The US and other governments have reportedly been impacted, too.

Microsoft explains that certain features of services "that interact with Exchange Online and email services are impacted." So, it looks like Exchange Online could be the culprit. This is the back-end of Microsoft services that use calendars, tasks, emails, and so on.

Affected services include MS365 admin center, apps, Education features, Copilot, Defender for Office 365, Defender XDR, Fabric, Graph, Intune, Planner, Power Apps, Purview, some elements of Teams, To Do, SharePoint Online, Universal Print, and Windows 365.

In other words, a very extensive list. It's also a list that a bunch of institutions and companies rely on to manage their day-to-day, thus why this is such a big deal.

The latest update from Microsoft, at the time of writing, explains:

"Recovery actions are ongoing and have progressed in phases across affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure. Global telemetry and customer reports show incremental improvement in several workloads; however, service health remains variable and capacity has not yet fully returned to baseline.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"Network and traffic-management actions remain active. To protect email during recovery, we’re continuing to prioritize queue and backlog processing, and the email timeout window has been extended to 48 hours to preserve delayed messages.

"At this time, we have no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident. We will continue to treat this with urgency until full mitigation, and we will share a full Post-Incident Report with root cause and defense-in-depth actions after mitigation is complete."

That there is "no evidence of malicious activity" as the cause is promising, but it doesn't stop this from being a severe event that's causing a ton of problems in a ton of countries.

This is the big risk of relying on a single kind of service for all your important online dealings. We saw the same risk bear fruit last year with a global AWS outage that took out a load of online services for a while, and recently we saw similarly widespread issues as a result of PHP vulnerabilities.

We're seeing more and more as time goes on that services from big, usually-reliable companies aren't immune to catastrophe. Let's hope Microsoft figures this one out ASAP.

#3767. GTA 6 reportedly has 55 Achievements/Trophies, more than both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 had at launch

GTA 6 is due to release on the 19th November on PS5, and Xbox Series X/S, and ahead of the highly-anticipated launch of Rockstar's latest sandbox adventure, people just can't get enough information about the game. To that end, overnight, we saw our latest leak: the game will have 55 Trophies/Achievements.

In a now-deleted tweet from (in)famous Rockstar dataminer, TexFunz2 - re-posted by the Twitter account iGrandTheftAuto - it appears the game will have 55 individual rewards for completing certain tasks and missions. At the time of writing, we don't know specifically what these challenges are, but it seems none of them will be attached to the online version of the game; the base game launches without GTA Online, and so we can safely assume that all these rewards will be for the single-player only content. GTA Online will drop sometime in 2027, according to Twitch's CEO.

If you've been paying attention to previous Rockstar titles, you'll know that Grand Theft Auto 5 launched with 51 Achievements/Trophies - again, all single-player - and Red Dead Redemption 2 launched with 52. So the latest game has more than either game got at launch - and I can tell you from experience, getting Platinum in either title was a very time-consuming experience. Expect the same to be true here, too.

It's worth highlighting that GTA 5 did, eventually, get more Achievements and Trophies: the GTA Online content upped the complete total to 78, adding 27 new challenges to complete. I would expect GTA 6 to do the same… whenever the PC version of GTA comes out, or GTA Online lands in the new game (it's possible both could happen at the same time).

Recently, we heard why a former Rockstar Games tech director thinks GTA 6 could be coming to PC sooner than you'd expect (mostly thanks to AI clones), when we can expect the pre-load of the game (10th November), and how big the final game install is expected to be (210GB). The final game is expected to be so big and dense with detail that no single Rockstar employee has seen the entire game, meaning there are plenty of easter eggs and ridiculous things to discover.

#3766. Rasen, out in early access now, is a PvP focused take on Dark Souls that borrows one of fighting games' best techy tricks

The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being said, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just launched into early access.

To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things. For one, it looks more like it leans a tad towards Sekiro with a blades-only kind of affair, whether that be big or small. And blades a plenty they have, ranging from your classic sword, to scythes, to halberds and all sorts. It's a much flashier looking affair too, with fancy slashing effects that seem to buff moves and a pace that seems much faster than Souls games tend to be.

You can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat! And best of all, unusually for a 3D arena fighter, it has rollback netcode. For those unfamiliar, and to try and explain it simply, this is essentially a bit of tech you'll find in predominantly 2D fighting games that predicts every possible input you could make in a given moment, helping to reduce lag time and allow for tighter matches (and less rage quitting).

That's a bit harder to do in a 3D environment given that you have a lot more options at your disposal when it comes to movement, so if it works that's some impressive stuff! And we could all quite easily find out together, as a demo for Rasen is available to try out. Or, alternatively, you can just pick it up whole hog on Steam right now, as it's available in early access.

Netflix has announced that Planeswalker, an animated series based on Magic: The Gathering, will debut in 2027. The first sneak peek doesn't show much, but it does suggest that the show is taking several pages from the streamer's wildly popular League of Legends series, Arcane.

The series "chronicles the fierce clash between formidable mages known as Planeswalkers. At the center of this struggle for power and survival burns Chandra, a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts and haunted by her past," according to the official synopsis.

"Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence. As the line between victory and annihilation grows thinner, a single spark determines the fate of thousands of worlds."

The video above is filled with concept and previsualization clips, but there are a few seconds of what appears to be near-final animation and, well, it's tough to deny a clear Arcane influence here in the character design and animation style. The series is being created by animation studio Digic Pictures, which has previously made cutscenes for games including Assassin's Creed Shadows and Call of Duty: Vanguard, and led several episodes of Amazon's Secret Level series.

Terry Matalas, who served as showrunner for VisionQuest and seasons 2 and 3 of Star Trek: Picard, will be showrunner for Planeswalker. Cindy Appel, who wrote episodes for both those shows, serves as co-showrunner. Patrick Osborne is supervising director and executive producer.

Netflix has been trying to get a Magic: The Gathering series underway since at least 2019, when the streamer announced that the Russo brothers were attached to the project. Whatever vision they had for the series seemingly fell through, as it was five years before we heard about it again – this time, led by Matalas.

In the meantime, check out our guides to the best shows on Netflix and the best movies on Netflix to find out what you should be streaming today.

#3764. Ads are coming to Xbox Cloud Gaming, and an executive thinks this is the only way to avoid ‘dramatic’ price increases in the industry

Advertisements in subscription services are nothing new. Netflix, Amazon, and every other company out there has some sort of ad-supported tier, which is often way cheaper or even entirely free depending on the service and how aggressive the ads are. However, gaming is a different beast, and we companies haven’t found ways to implement them outside the mobile space, where they remain on a quid-pro-quo basis anyway.

But that is slowly changing with the prevalence of subscriptions, and Xbox Cloud Gaming has just received an ad-based free edition players can hop onto without paying a single dime. Xbox Cloud Gaming has long been in decline and probably quite expensive for Microsoft to run and sustain, which led to time limits implemented across every Game Pass tier. With ads, things could turn the tide on Microsoft’s cloud gaming service and, according to Xbox general manager Jonathan Stringfield, potentially avert inevitable price hikes throughout the industry.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Stringfield predicts that, in the coming years, the games industry will inevitably be faced with rising costs and sustainability issues, which will then produce “dramatic” results whereby the costs will be offloaded to the end-user.

“Either of two things need to happen if we want to stick with the model as it exists today: We either need to dramatically increase the price of games, which I don’t think would be terribly popular with folks, or we need to find other mechanisms to allow access,” Stringfield said to Games Beat. One of these “other mechanisms” is, of course, ads.

“When we talk about advertising—and things that are adjacent to it that amount to recurrent revenue, whether it’s subscriptions or otherwise—what this allows for is an alternative,” he explained.

Stringfield prefaced these comments by saying advertising definitely cannot work in every game and probably not even every console or platform, and it isn’t necessarily going to be hammered into everything under the sun. However, they are to be viewed as a potential way to offset costs without extracting more money out of the end-user via higher prices. The very existence of premium platforms, and quite popular ones at that, whose sole stated purpose is to delete ads, does run counter to this somewhat.

People are very obviously willing to pay not to see ads or be interrupted during their viewing or gaming, so it remains to be seen if or how advertisements can be used in gaming broadly, outside of the limited scope of ad-based subscription services. Maybe we will all end up on the cloud eventually (Sam Altman does seem keen on the idea) and thus be forced to watch ads and, like Sony’s patent says, even be made to stand up and scream the product’s name on the screen to be given the ability to continue.

Grim ideas, and I hope they never come true.

#3763. Dungeons in World of Warcraft: Forever get a huge XP buff, but power-levellers shouldn't celebrate just yet

World of Warcraft: Forever has received a massive buff to the XP drop-rates of dungeon mobs (enemies), which should make running these instances multiple times feel more rewarding - and may revive an older levelling strategy.

This buff is a 50 percent increase in experience from all mobs killed inside all dungeons. As detailed in this World of Warcraft forum post, community manager Kaivax wrote that this change has been made "so it feels better to go back in for more runs". They don't outright say this is in response to community feedback, but the subject has been a hot topic since the beta.

World of Warcraft: Forever developers have spoken in the past about the decision to deliberately bring down dungeon mob XP to disincentivise power-levelling in dungeons. The idea was that by doing this, people would be encouraged to actually go out into the world and explore it, rather than hopping from instance to instance until they reached max level.

Sadly, a side effect of this change is that doing a dungeon more than once could feel unrewarding. Playing it once is great, as you get to complete lots of quests that reward guaranteed items and XP. However, if you go back again, you don't get these, so your only source of progression comes from a heavily decreased XP rate.

Some quests exacerbate this issue. Dungeons like Wailing Caverns and especially Blackfathom Deeps have a quest that can't really be completed in one run due to a reliance on drop rates for items you need, and having to fight for drops with the rest of your dungeon party. Having to go back to complete this used to suck, and now it sucks less!

So does this mean farming dungeons to power-level is back? Maybe, but it still won't be nearly as efficient as it was in older versions of Classic WoW. The current mob XP rates, after this buff, will still only be 36 percent of the original Classic rate - a third. Given how fast you can level by doing quests out in the world, it seems dungeon farming isn't due for a comeback just yet.

After an especially smooth launch, World of Warcraft: Forever has become the biggest launch in the series' history, beating out Wrath of the Lich King, Cataclysm, and all the other past expansion launches. The developers have been quick to hotfix things on the fly, including a change that left PvP battlegrounds heavily advantaged for the Horde.

#3762. Forage and fight for ingredients in a magical 1960s Italy and whip up some tasty meals Cooking Mama style in The Snackbar at the End of the World

If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

First up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

The other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only announced this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.
